decisive_items: severe sweating confined to his right arm and thoracic area
decreased surface temperature over the right arm and right thorax corresponding to dermatomes C5–T12
dense infiltrates in the ventral subpleural regions of the right upper and middle lobes
response.rationale: Pancoast tumor best explains the enlarging subpleural upper-lobe infiltrates, pleural friction rub, and ipsilateral sympathetic overactivity with sweating and coolness; absence of Horner signs and negative biopsy do not exclude an apical/upper-lobe tumor invading the sympathetic chain, whereas infection/empyema lack microbial and antibiotic response and CRPS/Sjögren/Horner do not account for the lung-pleural process.

rejected.why: No cavitation, no organisms on BAL, and no response to antibiotics; autonomic asymmetry is unexplained.
No pleural fluid collection or empyema is described, no organisms were found, and antibiotics failed.
No sicca or autoimmune features; interstitial pneumonia alone is insufficient and does not explain unilateral autonomic findings.
Pupils were equal and reactive with no ptosis, directly contradicting Horner's syndrome; hyperhidrosis is opposite of Horner anhidrosis.
Explains sweating and temperature asymmetry but not the enlarging lung infiltrates or pleural rub, and there is no trauma or typical CRPS features.
